data.title: MaxLinear climbs 15% amid infrastructure and data-center focus
data.description:
MaxLinear (MXL), a fabless semiconductor designer, rallied just over 15% on Friday, closing at $105.93 after gaining $13.81 on the day.

The gain extended a recovery that has built over the past several weeks, as the company's infrastructure and data-center product lines drew renewed investor attention. Volume reached approximately 4.28 million shares, nearly one and a half times the one-month average.

MXL has advanced about 87% over the past month. This included periodic strong one-session gains, including a 10% rise on September 25 and advances of about 8% on both September 17 and 18.

data.title: Nike seeks supply chain overhaul to improve profitability -- report
data.description:
Still reeling from the fallout from disappointing fiscal first-quarter results and another turn lower in the company’s share price, Nike (NKE) is now exploring ways to improve profitability by streamlining its supply chain and breaking with a 50-year trend of owning its own distribution network.

During a meeting with employees on Friday cited by Bloomberg, Nike (NKE) COO Venky Alagirisamy said the company aims to make a “more flexible, more responsive, and more efficient supply chain” and move towards a model to “leverage partnerships.”

Alagirisamy added that while manufacturing in Vietnam and China will remain "significant," Nike (NKE) is looking to "nearshore" sourcing for its North America and EMEA markets, a strategy the company had previously discussed prior to Thursday’s results.

While profits improved during the fiscal first quarter, the gains came from cost efficiencies rather than higher sales, momentum that could be interrupted by the recent spike in oil futures and its likely impact on transportation costs. By moving manufacturing closer to end markets, Nike (NKE) can mitigate the volatility in transportation costs. 

During the company’s earnings call with analysts, chief financial officer David Denton noted efforts to improve efficiencies, simplify operations, and increase productivity by “directing more resources towards the consumer, sport, product innovation, and growth opportunities with the greatest long-term potential.”

Nike (NKE) shares ended lower for a fourth consecutive day.

data.title: SA analyst: Yields could soon ‘roll over’ as stocks rally
data.description:
Wall Street climbed Friday after a cooler-than-expected September nonfarm payrolls report helped support equities and eased some pressure surrounding interest rates.

Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research pointed to the Nasdaq Composite’s (COMP:IND) latest record as evidence that stocks are absorbing elevated Treasury yields. 

“This week the Nasdaq made a new all-time high, thumbing its nose at the apparent crisis in yields,” King stated.

He also highlighted strength in the Russell 2000 (RTY), noting that both indexes are typically sensitive to interest rates. Their gains, he argued, suggest bond yields could soon begin declining. 

“Together with the Russell 2000 also being green on the week,” King said, “we conclude that yields are soon to roll over.” 

The U.S. one-year Treasury note yield declined during the week, providing an early indication that longer-term yields could eventually follow. 

Meanwhile, the weaker payrolls data reinforced expectations that economic conditions may allow pressure on rates to ease. 

King said the Nasdaq’s performance was particularly notable given prevailing investor pessimism. “Amidst a sea of dreadful sentiment,” he stated, the QQQ’s new all-time high provides “further supporting evidence” for his expectation of a rally into year-end.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count drops 1 in latest Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. declined by 1 to 598, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. added 1 to 456 in the week ended September 25, while gas rigs fell by 2 to 133 and miscellaneous rigs remained unchanged at 9.

The total rig count was up by 49, or 8.9%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 34, or 8%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 15, or 12.7%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin totaled 269, the Eagle Ford count was 41, and the Williston Basin came in at 30, all staying flat during the past week.

data.title: U.S. equities ended well into the green as cooler payrolls data arrived
data.description:
Wall Street closed in the green on Friday after the September nonfarm payrolls report came in cooler than economists expected.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended +0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) closed +0.7%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished +1.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, 10 of the 11 segments ended in positive territory and were led by consumer discretionary. At the other end of the spectrum, healthcare was the weakest performer.

“This week the Nasdaq made a new all-time high, thumbing its nose at the apparent crisis in yields.  Together with the Russell 2000 also being green on the week, and these two indices being rather rates-sensitive usually, we conclude that yields are soon to roll over,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

U.S. employers added just 29K jobs in September, well short of the 85K consensus figure and a sharp slowdown from August’s downwardly revised gain of 133K (from 162K), the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday. 

“Not only were the 29K jobs created in Sept. below expectations, but as I predicted last month, July and Aug. were revised down by 31K and 29K respectively. My guess is that all three months will ultimately be revised even lower. We have a weak labor market with strong inflation,” Peter Schiff of Europac stated. 

Treasury yields were lower early on but pushed back up at the close. The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.83%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) moved higher by 3 basis points to 5.28%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) pushed up 2 basis points to 5.62%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of ON Semiconductor (ON) advanced +5.8%, while shares of Seagate Technology (STX) fell -10.2%.
